title: Schema-adaptive proxy and zero-downtime reindexing plan for embedding dimension changes
creator: Aisha Nadar
description: Summary: We need a rollout plan and lightweight runtime proxy that allows the embeddings service to change vector dimensionality (grow or shrink) with zero or minimal downtime for reranking customers. This ticket defines a schema-adaptive proxy approach that provides: 1) transparent client negotiation for vector schema, 2) on-the-fly compatibility transformations (pad/truncate/orthonormal projection), 3) asynchronous streaming reindex with tombstones and incremental swap, and 4) KV-cache coherence and cache-warm strategies to preserve latency SLOs.
background: Recent requests to switch to a 384->512 embedding dimension (and occasional experiments with 256 dims for cost-sensitive workloads) exposed three problems: client-server schema mismatch errors, expensive bulk reindex operations causing CPU/GPU contention, and increased cold-latency due to KV cache invalidations. Existing playbooks focus on offline reindex windows; we need a production-safe, live migration capability for both hosted and Dedicated deployments.
approach: 1) Implement a lightweight 'schema-adaptive proxy' layer in front of embedding storage and reranking endpoints. The proxy will accept client-declared vector schema via a handshake and record client capabilities. 2) Provide deterministic on-the-fly transform modules: PAD_ZERO, TRUNCATE_LOW_VARIANCE, and PCA_PROJ (trained projection matrix) to map between source and target dims when safe. 3) Introduce an async streaming reindexer: reads old index, writes new index shards incrementally, emits tombstones and proxy routing hints when a doc is served from the new index. 4) KV cache strategy: mark cache entry versions, keep a fast-path lookup that prefers cached transformed vectors where available; use background jobs to refill cache hotspots from new index. 5) Cutover flow: staged rollouts by customer cohort, shadow verification, and incremental primary swap shard-by-shard with automatic rollback on regression thresholds.
tradeoffs: - On-the-fly transforms (pad/truncate) are cheap but can degrade reranking quality for some queries; PCA_PROJ preserves semantics better but requires training and extra memory for the projection matrix. - Streaming reindex reduces peak load but prolongs migration period. - Proxy adds an extra network hop and small latency delta; mitigated with in-proxy cache and colocated deployments for Dedicated customers.
implementation_steps: Design handshake protocol: client vector_schema header + compatibility level negotiation
Build proxy routing shim with transform plugin interface (go/rust) and unit tests
Create transform library: PAD_ZERO, TRUNCATE_LOW_VARIANCE, PCA_PROJ with metrics for quality delta
Develop streaming reindexer with backpressure, shard-level cutover markers, and tombstone events
Add cache-version metadata and fast-path transformed-cache support in serving runtime
Add observability: per-client schema map, transform hit-rate, transform quality metrics (nDCG delta), reindex progress dashboard
Run canary on non-critical tenants, measure latency P95 and rerank quality against benchmark prompts
Prepare runbook and rollback plan; coordinate with Support and Solutions for customer communications
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts mixed-dimension requests without 4xx errors and returns consistent responses
End-to-end reranking quality degradation <= 1.5% nDCG on benchmark set for PAD_ZERO; PCA_PROJ target <= 0.5%
Migration can proceed without >10% increase in P95 latency across targeted tenants
Streaming reindex can fill target index at sustained throughput required for medium customers (>= 1M docs/day) with throttling controls
Ability to rollback to previous index within 30 minutes of failed cutover
Automated dashboards show per-tenant schema distribution and reindex progress
monitoring_and_metrics: Track: transform_hit_rate, transform_quality_nDCG, per-tenant P50/P95 latency delta, index_reindex_throughput, reindex_backpressure_events, cache_miss_ratio_post-migration. Alerts: quality degradation >2% nDCG for >10m, P95 latency spike >20% sustained >5m, reindex task failure rate >1%.
rollback_plan: If quality or latency thresholds are breached during canary or staged rollout: 1) pause reindexer and halt cutovers, 2) proxy switches routing back to old index shards via cutover markers, 3) invalidate transformed-cache entries and enable warm-fill of original vectors, 4) create incident with engineering and notify affected customers. Automated rollback script will be tested in staging.
security_considerations: Projection matrices and transformation metadata must be treated as model artifacts; restrict access via KMS-backed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments. Ensure no unencrypted vectors are logged; follow existing KMS and audit logging patterns (integrate with platform KMS/HSM).
